# Security verification checklist

Every OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 level 1 and 2 requirement (253) and every MASVS control (24), with its status in this repository and the evidence for it. Reviewed 2026-10-12.

Statuses:

- **Met**: Implemented and verified in this repository.
- **Partial**: Partly implemented; the note says what is missing and when it lands.
- **Deployment**: Depends on production infrastructure set up in phase 12; the note says what the application already does.
- **Accepted**: A documented deviation with compensating controls (ADR-048).
- **N/A**: The platform does not use the technology or feature.

To change a status, edit `docs/security/standards/mapping.json` and run `pnpm security:checklist`. CI runs it with `--check`, so the mapping, the evidence paths and this page cannot drift apart. Accepted deviations and their compensating controls are recorded in ADR-048.

## Open items

Everything that is not met or not applicable, for planning:

| ID | Status | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V4.1.2 | Deployment | Edge configuration (phase 12): redirect HTTP to HTTPS only on the web and console hosts; the API host answers HTTPS only. HSTS preload already covers all three. |
| V4.2.1 | Deployment | Node's HTTP parser rejects messages with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding; load balancer settings come with phase 12. |
| V6.3.3 | Accepted | Staff must use MFA. For travellers MFA is offered but optional; compensating controls and the rationale are in ADR-048. |
| V6.5.5 | Accepted | Texted codes live 5 minutes. TOTP uses 30-second steps and accepts one step of clock drift (RFC 6238), each step once; see ADR-048. |
| V7.2.4 | Accepted | Every sign-in, including MFA completion, issues new tokens. Re-authentication and step-up raise assurance on the current session without rotating it; see ADR-048. |
| V11.5.1 | Accepted | Tokens and secrets are 256-bit from the CSPRNG. Voucher codes carry about 99 bits; see ADR-048. |
| V12.1.1 | Deployment | The edge TLS policy (TLS 1.2 and 1.3, 1.3 preferred) comes with phase 12. Node clients already refuse anything below TLS 1.2. |
| V12.1.2 | Deployment | Cipher suites are set with the edge TLS policy in phase 12. |
| V12.2.1 | Deployment | HSTS with preload is already on every response; the edge serves TLS only (phase 12). |
| V12.2.2 | Deployment | Publicly trusted certificates are issued at the edge in phase 12. |
| V12.3.1 | Deployment | The application refuses plaintext in production for providers, Postgres, Redis, the worker-to-API hop, OTLP and SMTP, except declared private paths. ClamAV has no TLS and must run on the same host or a private network (phase 12). |
| V12.3.3 | Deployment | The worker must call the API over https in production. The web and console servers' API URLs are set to https in phase 12. |
| V12.3.4 | Deployment | Internal certificates and CA pinning for managed services are set up in phase 12. |
| V13.2.1 | Partial | The worker authenticates to the internal API with a static bearer token over TLS, and the services use password credentials for Postgres and Redis. Phase 12 replaces these with workload identity and short-lived credentials. |
| V13.2.2 | Deployment | Separate least-privilege database roles for the application and migrations, and scoped cloud identities, come with phase 12. |
| V13.2.5 | Deployment | Egress network policy in phase 12. |
| V13.3.1 | Deployment | Secrets live in the cloud secret manager (phase 12); the application reads them only from the environment. |
| V13.3.2 | Deployment | Per-service access to secrets is set up with the secret manager in phase 12. |
| V13.4.1 | Deployment | Container images are built without source control metadata in phase 12. |
| V13.4.4 | Deployment | The API answers TRACE with 404 (checked 2026-10-12). The edge blocks TRACE on every host in phase 12. |
| V14.2.1 | Accepted | Tokens travel in headers, bodies or URL fragments. The exception is signed document links, whose query carries a 5-minute signature for one document; see ADR-048. |
| V16.4.2 | Deployment | The audit log is append-only in the database. Access to the log service is configured in phase 12. |
| V16.4.3 | Deployment | Logs leave each container on stdout; shipping to a separate log service is part of phase 12. |
| MASVS-NETWORK-2 | Accepted | No certificate pinning; see ADR-048. |
| MASVS-CODE-1 | Accepted | Targets Android API 36; supports Android 7.0 and iOS 15.1 and later for reach in the primary market; see ADR-048. |
| MASVS-RESILIENCE-1 | Partial | App Attest and Play Integrity are wired with report and strict modes; real verifiers need the owner's Apple and Google accounts (open owner question). |
| MASVS-RESILIENCE-2 | Accepted | No anti-tampering beyond attestation; see ADR-048. |
| MASVS-RESILIENCE-3 | Accepted | No obfuscation beyond Hermes bytecode; the bundle holds no secrets (scanned); see ADR-048. |
| MASVS-RESILIENCE-4 | Accepted | No anti-debugging; see ADR-048. |
| MASVS-PRIVACY-3 | Partial | The privacy policy text and the store privacy labels come from the owner (open owner question). |

| V13.4.5 | 2 | Verify that documentation (such as for internal APIs) and monitoring endpoints are not exposed unless explicitly intended. | Met | `apps/api/src/app.setup.ts`<br>`apps/worker/src/health-server.ts` | No API documentation UI in any environment; the worker's health port is internal; metrics are pushed over OTLP, not exposed. |

## ASVS: V14 Data Protection

| ID | L | Requirement | Status | Evidence | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V14.1.1 | 2 | Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels. This includes data that is only encoded and therefore easily decoded, such as Base64 strings or the plaintext payload inside a JWT. Protection levels need to take into account any data protection and privacy regulations and standards which the application is required to comply with. | Met | `docs/security/data-classification.md` |  |
| V14.1.2 | 2 | Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements. This must include (but not be limited to) requirements related to general encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, database-level encryption, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies to be used, and other confidentiality requirements. | Met | `docs/security/data-classification.md` |  |
| V14.2.1 | 1 | Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token. | Accepted | `docs/decisions/ADR-048-security-verification-and-accepted-risks.md`<br>`apps/api/src/visa/visa-documents.service.ts` | Tokens travel in headers, bodies or URL fragments. The exception is signed document links, whose query carries a 5-minute signature for one document; see ADR-048. |
| V14.2.2 | 2 | Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use. | Met | `apps/api/src/app.setup.ts`<br>`apps/web/lib/api.ts` | API responses are Cache-Control no-store; the website caches only public reads. |
| V14.2.3 | 2 | Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties (e.g., user trackers) to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control. | Met | `apps/web/lib/cookie-catalog.ts`<br>`docs/security/logging-inventory.md` | No third-party trackers; error reports are scrubbed; optional categories need consent. |
| V14.2.4 | 2 | Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies, are implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level. | Met | `docs/security/data-classification.md`<br>`packages/shared/src/log-redaction.ts`<br>`apps/api/src/crypto/encryption-contexts.ts` |  |
| V14.3.1 | 1 | Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage, such as the browser DOM, after the client or session is terminated. The 'Clear-Site-Data' HTTP response header field may be able to help with this but the client-side should also be able to clear up if the server connection is not available when the session is terminated. | Met | `apps/web/components/account/use-account.ts`<br>`apps/mobile/src/lib/session.ts` | Sign-out clears tokens, booking tokens and cached personal data on the web and in the app. |
| V14.3.2 | 2 | Verify that the application sets sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields (i.e., Cache-Control: no-store) so that sensitive data is not cached in browsers. | Met | `apps/api/src/app.setup.ts` | Cache-Control no-store on every API response; private pages render their data client-side from the API. |
| V14.3.3 | 2 | Verify that data stored in browser storage (such as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or cookies) does not contain sensitive data, with the exception of session tokens. | Met | `apps/web/lib/cookie-catalog.ts` | Browser storage holds preferences, recent searches, guest booking tokens (session-scoped) and, for one tab, a surname typed for the add-on lookup. |

## ASVS: V15 Secure Coding and Architecture

| ID | L | Requirement | Status | Evidence | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V15.1.1 | 1 | Verify that application documentation defines risk based remediation time frames for 3rd party component versions with vulnerabilities and for updating libraries in general, to minimize the risk from these components. | Met | `SECURITY.md`<br>`docs/security/dependency-exceptions.md` |  |
| V15.1.2 | 2 | Verify that an inventory catalog, such as software bill of materials (SBOM), is maintained of all third-party libraries in use, including verifying that components come from pre-defined, trusted, and continually maintained repositories. | Met | `.github/workflows/security.yml`<br>`pnpm-lock.yaml` | CycloneDX SBOM on every security run; packages come only from the npm registry with a frozen lockfile. |
| V15.1.3 | 2 | Verify that the application documentation identifies functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding. This must include how to prevent a loss of availability due to overusing this functionality and how to avoid a situation where building a response takes longer than the consumer's timeout. Potential defenses may include asynchronous processing, using queues, and limiting parallel processes per user and per application. | Met | `docs/security/business-limits.md` |  |
| V15.2.1 | 1 | Verify that the application only contains components which have not breached the documented update and remediation time frames. | Met | `.github/workflows/security.yml`<br>`docs/security/dependency-exceptions.md` | CI fails on high or critical advisories; exceptions are reviewed monthly. |
| V15.2.2 | 2 | Verify that the application has implemented defenses against loss of availability due to functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding, based on the documented security decisions and strategies for this. | Met | `docs/security/business-limits.md`<br>`apps/api/src/suppliers/circuit-breaker.ts` |  |
| V15.2.3 | 2 | Verify that the production environment only includes functionality that is required for the application to function, and does not expose extraneous functionality such as test code, sample snippets, and development functionality. | Met | `apps/api/src/config/env.schema.ts` | Production refuses mock adapters, the demo seed and development tokens; test code is not part of the builds. |
| V15.3.1 | 1 | Verify that the application only returns the required subset of fields from a data object. For example, it should not return an entire data object, as some individual fields should not be accessible to users. | Met | `apps/api/src/contract/contract.interceptor.ts` |  |
| V15.3.2 | 2 | Verify that where the application backend makes calls to external URLs, it is configured to not follow redirects unless it is intended functionality. | Met | `docs/security/external-communications.md` | Every outbound HTTP client uses redirect: error. |
| V15.3.3 | 2 | Verify that the application has countermeasures to protect against mass assignment attacks by limiting allowed fields per controller and action, e.g., it is not possible to insert or update a field value when it was not intended to be part of that action. | Met | `apps/api/src/contract/contract.ts` | Zod drops fields that a body schema does not list. |
| V15.3.4 | 2 | Verify that all proxying and middleware components transfer the user's original IP address correctly using trusted data fields that cannot be manipulated by the end user, and the application and web server use this correct value for logging and security decisions such as rate limiting, taking into account that even the original IP address may not be reliable due to dynamic IPs, VPNs, or corporate firewalls. | Met | `apps/api/src/app.setup.ts` | TRUST_PROXY_HOPS decides how much of X-Forwarded-For to trust; the edge is configured to overwrite it in phase 12. |
| V15.3.5 | 2 | Verify that the application explicitly ensures that variables are of the correct type and performs strict equality and comparator operations. This is to avoid type juggling or type confusion vulnerabilities caused by the application code making an assumption about a variable type. | Met | `packages/config/eslint/base.mjs`<br>`apps/api/src/contract/contract.ts` | TypeScript strict mode, eqeqeq, and schema-typed inputs. |
| V15.3.6 | 2 | Verify that JavaScript code is written in a way that prevents prototype pollution, for example, by using Set() or Map() instead of object literals. | Met | `apps/api/src/contract/contract.ts` | Inputs become new objects through Zod; lookups use Map and Set; no deep merges of user input. |
| V15.3.7 | 2 | Verify that the application has defenses against HTTP parameter pollution attacks, particularly if the application framework makes no distinction about the source of request parameters (query string, body parameters, cookies, or header fields). | Met | `apps/api/src/contract/contract.ts` | Body, query and path each have their own schema; repeated parameters fail validation. |

UTC is recommended to ensure consistency across distributed systems and to prevent confusion during daylight saving time transitions. | Met | `docs/security/logging-inventory.md` | UTC timestamps everywhere; host clocks are kept in sync by the managed runtime. |
| V16.2.3 | 2 | Verify that the application only stores or broadcasts logs to the files and services that are documented in the log inventory. | Met | `docs/security/logging-inventory.md` |  |
| V16.2.4 | 2 | Verify that logs can be read and correlated by the log processor that is in use, preferably by using a common logging format. | Met | `apps/api/src/logging/logging.module.ts` | JSON lines with a request id shared across services. |

| V16.3.1 | 2 | Verify that all authentication operations are logged, including successful and unsuccessful attempts. | V16.3.2 | 2 | Verify that failed authorization attempts are logged. For L3, this must include logging all authorization decisions, including logging when sensitive data is accessed (without logging the sensitive data itself). | Met | `apps/api/src/auth/permissions.guard.ts`<br>`apps/api/src/audit/audit.service.ts` |  |
| V16.3.3 | 2 | Verify that the application logs the security events that are defined in the documentation and also logs attempts to bypass the security controls, such as input validation, business logic, and anti-automation. | Met | `apps/api/src/logging/logging.module.ts`<br>`docs/security/logging-inventory.md` | Validation failures, rate limits and bot-check failures are logged; 403 and 429 at warn. |
| V16.3.4 | 2 | Verify that the application logs unexpected errors and security control failures such as backend TLS failures. | Met | `apps/api/src/common/problem-details.ts`<br>`docs/security/logging-inventory.md` |  |
| V16.4.1 | 2 | Verify that all logging components appropriately encode data to prevent log injection. | Met | `apps/api/src/logging/logging.module.ts` | JSON encoding escapes control characters. |

| V16.4.3 | 2 | Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a logically separate system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. | V16.5.2 | 2 | Verify that the application continues to operate securely when external resource access fails, for example, by using patterns such as circuit breakers or graceful degradation. | Met | `apps/api/src/suppliers/circuit-breaker.ts`<br>`apps/api/src/search/supplier-runner.ts` |  |

## ASVS: V17 WebRTC

| ID | L | Requirement | Status | Evidence | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V17.1.1 | 2 | Verify that the Traversal Using Relays around NAT (TURN) service only allows access to IP addresses that are not reserved for special purposes (e.g., internal networks, broadcast, loopback). Note that this applies to both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. | N/A |  | No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers. |
| V17.2.1 | 2 | Verify that the key for the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) certificate is managed and protected based on the documented policy for management of cryptographic keys. | N/A |  | No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers. |
| V17.2.2 | 2 | Verify that the media server is configured to use and support approved Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) cipher suites and a secure protection profile for the DTLS Extension for establishing keys for the Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (DTLS-SRTP). | N/A |  | No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers. |
| V17.2.3 | 2 | Verify that Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) authentication is checked at the media server to prevent Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) injection attacks from leading to either a Denial of Service condition or audio or video media insertion into media streams. | N/A |  | No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers. |
| V17.2.4 | 2 | Verify that the media server is able to continue processing incoming media traffic when encountering malformed Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) packets. | N/A |  | No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers. |
| V17.3.1 | 2 | Verify that the signaling server is able to continue processing legitimate incoming signaling messages during a flood attack. This should be achieved by implementing rate limiting at the signaling level. | N/A |  | No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers. |
| V17.3.2 | 2 | Verify that the signaling server is able to continue processing legitimate signaling messages when encountering malformed signaling message that could cause a denial of service condition. This could include implementing input validation, safely handling integer overflows, preventing buffer overflows, and employing other robust error-handling techniques. | N/A |  | No WebRTC, TURN, media or signalling servers. |
